title: Linear trends do not reduce held-cycle error for low orbital harmonics of KIC 3749404 in Kepler Q2 to Q16
abstract: We test whether linear changes in the known KIC 3749404 heartbeat waveform predict held-out Kepler observing cycles. Across 72 choices of flux product, time baseline, period, harmonic range and amplitude scaling, a linear model has 6.97 to 16.45 percent more prediction error than a constant model. A season-plus-linear model also has more error than a season model. A residual-cut test retains the central null result. Known added harmonic trends improve linear prediction, but this control does not measure sensitivity to physical precession. This result applies to the tested coefficient models and does not reject the published precessing-binary model. No new planet, new signal or independent observation is reported. Code, accepted samples, exact source hashes, tables, figures and offline instructions are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-b5cea4dfeb47; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
